title: Adirondack guideboat
about: Rowboat of the Adirondacks, New York
blurb: A light rowboat developed in the 1840s in the Adirondacks, with spruce ribs and cedar planking fixed with copper tacks, light enough for one guide to carry between lakes.

title: Airstream
blurb: The rounded, riveted aluminium travel trailer that has gleamed along American highways since the 1930s.

title: Autozam AZ-1
blurb: The Autozam AZ-1 is a sports car which was manufactured by Mazda from October 1992 to October 1994 and sold under its Autozam brand. Suzuki provided the engine as well as the inspiration for the design. It is a two-seater kei car with a rear mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive layout and gullwing doors.

title: AWS Shopper
blurb: The AWS Shopper was a German Automobile manufactured in Berlin from 1973 to 1974. The first car was shown in 1970 and a few hand-built cars were made, but series production began in 1973. 1700 were made.

title: Barouche
blurb: A barouche or calèche is a large four-wheeled carriage designed for display and summer leisure driving. Drawn by a pair or team of horses, it has a canoe-shaped body with a folding leather hood over the rear seat.

title: Bilenky Cycle Works
blurb: Founded in 1983, Bilenky Cycle Works builds high-end handcrafted bikes in North Philadelphia.

title: BMW M3
about: High-performance version of the BMW 3 Series automobile
blurb: The BMW M3 is a high-performance version of the BMW 3 Series, developed by BMW's in-house motorsport division, BMW M GmbH. M3 models have been produced for every generation of 3 Series since the E30 M3 was introduced in 1986.

title: Brougham
blurb: A brougham is a 19th century four-wheeled carriage drawn by a single horse. It was named after the politician and jurist Lord Brougham, who had this type of carriage built to his specification by London coachbuilder Robinson & Cook in 1838.

title: Buggy
blurb: A buggy is an American lightweight four-wheeled carriage drawn by a single horse, though occasionally by two. Amish buggies are still regularly in use on the roadways of the United States. The word "buggy" has become a generic term for "carriage" in the United States.

title: Bull boat
about: Small boat of buffalo hide over a wooden frame
blurb: A small boat made by stretching a buffalo hide over a wooden frame, used by the Nueta people and by frontiersmen for travelling and fishing.

title: BYD Racco
about: Kei car produced by BYD Auto
blurb: The BYD Racco is a battery electric kei car manufactured by BYD Auto in 2026 for the Japanese market. It is the carmaker's attempt to making an electric kei car for the Japanese market and also the first and only one dedicated pure kei car model from a non-Japanese brand.

title: Cabriolet
blurb: A cabriolet is a light horse-drawn vehicle, with two wheels and a single horse. The carriage has a folding hood that can cover its two occupants, one of whom is the driver. It has a large rigid apron, upward-curving shafts, and usually a rear platform between the C springs for a groom.

title: Carriage
blurb: A carriage is a two- or four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle for passengers. Coaches are a special category within carriages; they are enclosed carriages with four corner posts and a fixed roof.

title: Chaise
blurb: A chaise, sometimes called shay, is a light two-wheeled carriage for one or two people. It may also have a folding hood. The coachmaker William Felton considered chaises to be a family of vehicles which included all two-wheel one-horse vehicles such as gigs and whiskies.

title: Charabanc
blurb: A charabanc or "char-à-banc" /ˈʃærəbæŋk/ is a type of horse-drawn vehicle and an early motor coach, usually open-topped, common in Britain during the early part of the 20th century. The term remains in use for some public service vehicles in a small number of countries.

title: Chariot
about: Carriage using animals to provide rapid motive power
blurb: A chariot is a type of two-wheeled vehicle with spoked wheels, driven by a charioteer, usually using horses to provide rapid motive power for usage in warfare. The oldest known chariots have been found in burials of the Sintashta culture in modern-day Chelyabinsk Oblast, Russia, dated to c.

title: Chevrolet Impala
blurb: The Chevrolet Impala is a full-size car that was built by Chevrolet for model years 1958 to 1985, 1994 to 1996, and 2000 to 2020. The Impala was Chevrolet's popular flagship passenger car and was among the better-selling American-made automobiles in the United States.

title: Chundan vallam
blurb: The long 'beaked boat' of Kerala, rowed by large crews in the Vallamkali boat races.

title: Citroën 2CV
blurb: A French economy car designed to carry a basket of eggs across a ploughed field without breaking one.

title: Coach
blurb: Coaches are horse-drawn carriages which are large, enclosed, four-wheeled, pulled by two or more horses, and controlled by a coachman or postilion. If driven by a coachman, there is a raised seat in front for a coachman called a box, box seat, or coach box.

title: Conestoga wagon
about: Covered freight wagon of the 18th and 19th centuries
blurb: A heavy horse-drawn freight wagon under hemp cloth stretched over hoops, first used by Pennsylvania Dutch settlers in the early 1700s, with a curved floor that kept the load in the middle.

title: Coracle
blurb: A coracle is a small, rounded, lightweight boat traditionally used in Wales, Ireland, particularly on the River Boyne, and Scotland, particularly on the River Spey. The word is also used for similar boats found in India, Vietnam, Iraq, and Tibet.

title: Cruiser bicycle
blurb: A cruiser bicycle, also known as a beach cruiser or motobike, is a bicycle that usually combines balloon tires, an upright seating posture, a single-speed drivetrain, and straightforward steel construction with expressive styling.

title: Daihatsu Copen
blurb: The Daihatsu Copen is a 2-door convertible kei car built by the Japanese car company Daihatsu. It debuted at the 1999 Tokyo Motor Show, as the Daihatsu Copen concept. The second generation model debuted as the Kopen at the 2013 Tokyo Motor Show.

title: Daihatsu Mira
blurb: The Daihatsu Mira was a kei-type city car built by Japanese car maker Daihatsu. It was built with a variety of options and chassis variations, with the latest variant having four models: Mira, Mira AVY, Mira Gino, and Mira VAN.

title: DMC DeLorean
blurb: The DMC DeLorean is a rear-engine, two-seat sports car manufactured and marketed by John DeLorean's DeLorean Motor Company for the American market from 1980 until 1982—ultimately the only car brought to market by the fledgling company.

title: Dodge Tomahawk
blurb: The Dodge Tomahawk was a non-street legal vehicle introduced in 2004 by Dodge at the North American International Auto Show, as a one-off concept, and later that year, DaimlerChrysler announced they would sell hand-built reproductions on order.

title: Dog sled
about: Sled pulled by one or more sled dogs
blurb: A dog sled or dog sleigh is a sled pulled by one or more sled dogs used to travel over ice and through snow, a practice known as mushing. Numerous types of sleds are used, depending on their function. They can be used for dog sled racing.

title: Dogcart
blurb: A dogcart is a two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle pulled by a single horse in shafts, or driven tandem. With seating for four, it was designed for sporting shooters and their gun dogs, with a louvred box under the driver's seat to contain dogs.

title: Ducati Panigale V4
blurb: The Ducati Panigale V4 is a sport bike with a 1,103 cc desmodromic 90° V4 engine introduced by Ducati in 2018 as the successor to the V-twin engined 1299.

title: Dugout canoe
about: Boat made from a hollowed tree
blurb: A dugout canoe or simply dugout is a boat made from a hollowed-out tree. Other names for this type of boat are logboat and monoxylon. Monoxylon is Greek – mono- + ξύλον xylon – and is mostly used in classic Greek texts. In German, they are called Einbaum.

title: Firefly Bicycles
blurb: Custom titanium and carbon high-performance bicycles, handmade in Boston, Massachusetts.

title: Gig
blurb: A gig is a light, two-wheeled open carriage with large wheels, a forward facing seat, and shafts for a single horse. The gig's body is constructed above the shafts, and it is entered from step-irons hanging from the shaft in front of the wheels.

title: Gondola
blurb: A flat-bottomed Venetian rowing boat, steered from the stern with a single oar.

title: Hackney carriage
blurb: A hackney or hackney carriage is a carriage or car for hire. A symbol of London and Britain, the black taxi is a common sight on the streets of London. The hackney carriages carry a roof sign TAXI that can be illuminated to indicate their availability for passengers.

title: Handcycle
blurb: A handcycle is a type of human-powered land vehicle powered by the arms rather than the legs, as on a bicycle. Most handcycles are tricycle in form, with two coasting rear wheels and one steerable powered front wheel. Despite usually having three wheels, they are also known as handbikes.

title: Hansom cab
blurb: The hansom cab is a two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle designed as a carriage for hire in London. First patented in 1834 by Joseph Hansom of England, and named the Hansom Safety Cab, it was designed to have a low centre of gravity to improve stability when maneuvering London's crowded streets, while…

title: Harley-Davidson Sportster
blurb: The Harley-Davidson Sportster is a line of motorcycles produced continuously since 1957 by Harley-Davidson. Sportster models are designated in Harley-Davidson's product code by beginning with "XL".

title: Hindustan Ambassador
about: Car made by Hindustan Motors from 1957 to 2014
blurb: Based on the Morris Oxford and built in India from 1957 to 2014, the rounded Ambassador was for decades India's taxi, family car and official car.

title: Hot air balloon
blurb: A wicker basket under a bag of heated air: the first technology to carry people into the sky.

title: Howdah
about: Carriage placed on the back of an elephant, camel, or other animal
blurb: A howdah or houdah also known as hathi howdah, is a carriage which is positioned on the back of an elephant, or occasionally some other animal, such as a camel, used most often in the past to carry wealthy people during progresses or processions, hunting or in warfare.

title: Ineos Grenadier
blurb: The Ineos Grenadier is an off-road utility vehicle designed and produced by Ineos Automotive. It went into production in October 2022.

title: Isetta
blurb: The Isetta is an Italian-designed microcar initially manufactured in 1953 by the Italian firm Iso SpA, and subsequently built under license in a number of different countries, including Argentina, Spain, Belgium, France, Brazil, Germany, and the United Kingdom.

title: Kawasaki Ninja H2
blurb: The Kawasaki Ninja H2 is a supercharged four-stroke hypersport-class motorcycle in the Ninja sports bike series manufactured by Kawasaki, featuring a variable-speed centrifugal supercharger.

title: Kawasaki Ninja ZX-10R
blurb: The Kawasaki Ninja ZX-10R is a motorcycle in the Ninja sport bike series from the Japanese manufacturer Kawasaki, the successor to the Ninja ZX-9R. It was originally released in 2004 and has been updated and revised throughout the years.

title: Kawasaki Ninja ZX-6R
blurb: The Kawasaki Ninja ZX-6R is a 600 cc class motorcycle in the Ninja sport bike series from the Japanese manufacturer Kawasaki. It was introduced in 1995, and has been constantly updated throughout the years in response to new products from Honda, Suzuki, and Yamaha.

title: Kei car
blurb: Kei car, short for kei-jidōsha, is a class of ultra-compact cars unique to the Japanese domestic market, and is the smallest category of expressway-legal motor vehicles in Japan. Other than passenger cars, Japanese automakers also make microvans and kei trucks within this legal category.

title: Kettuvallam
blurb: A Kerala houseboat with a thatched roof over a wooden hull, drifting along the backwaters.

title: KTM 390 series
blurb: The KTM 390 Series is a range of single-cylinder engine motorcycles assembled by Bajaj Auto, and KTM Asia Motorcycle Manufacturing, Inc. for the Austrian manufacturer KTM.

title: Lambretta
about: Brand name of Italian (mainly) motor scooters
blurb: Lambretta was a brand of motor scooters, manufactured in Milan, Italy, by Innocenti. The name is derived from the word Lambrate, the suburb of Milan named after the river Lambro which flows through the area, and where the factory was located.

title: Landau
blurb: A landau is a large four-wheeled carriage with a leather cover that can be folded down, essentially a coach with a falling top. The low shell of the landau provides maximal visibility of the occupants and their attire, a feature that makes a landau a popular choice for ceremonial occasions.

title: Lexus IS
blurb: The Lexus IS is a compact executive car sold by Lexus, a luxury division of Toyota, since 1998. The IS was originally sold under the Toyota Altezza nameplate in Japan from 1998 until 2005. The IS was introduced as an entry-level sport model positioned below the ES in the Lexus lineup.

title: Lexus LS
about: Full-size luxury sedan series produced by Lexus
blurb: The Lexus LS is a series of full-size luxury sedans that have served as the flagship model of Lexus, the luxury division of Toyota, since 1989. For the first four generations, all LS models featured V8 engines and were predominantly rear-wheel-drive.

title: Litter
about: Human-powered wheelless vehicle for the transport of persons
blurb: The litter, also known as a sedan chair, palanquin or dooly, is a class of wheelless vehicles, a type of human-powered transport, for the transport of people.

title: Maruti 800
about: City car made by Maruti Suzuki from 1983 to 2014
blurb: The little 800 cc car, based on the Suzuki Alto, that put India on wheels: about 2.87 million were built between 1983 and 2014.

title: Mazda MX-5
blurb: The Mazda MX-5 is a lightweight two-seat sports car manufactured and marketed by Mazda. While in most markets it is called the MX5, in Japan it is marketed as the Mazda Roadster or, previously, as the Eunos Roadster, and In the United States it is sold as the Mazda MX-5 Miata.

title: Mazda RX-7
blurb: The Mazda RX-7 is a sports car which was manufactured and marketed by Mazda from 1978 to 2002 across three generations. It has a front mid engine, rear-wheel-drive layout and uses a compact and lightweight Wankel rotary engine.

title: Mercedes-AMG GT
blurb: The Mercedes-AMG GT is a series of 2-door sports cars produced by German automobile manufacturer Mercedes-AMG. The car was introduced on 9 September 2014 and was officially unveiled to the public in October 2014 at the Paris Motor Show.

title: Mini
blurb: A tiny British car of 1959 that fitted four adults by turning its engine sideways.

title: Mitsubishi Pajero
blurb: The Mitsubishi Pajero is a full-size SUV manufactured and marketed globally by Mitsubishi Motors since 1981. It is also known as the Mitsubishi Montero in North America, Spain, and Latin America, and the Mitsubishi Shogun in the United Kingdom.

title: Moots
blurb: Handcrafted in Colorado since 1981, Moots builds titanium road, gravel and mountain bikes designed to last a lifetime.

title: Nissan GT-R
about: Sports car manufactured by Japanese automobile manufacturer Nissan
blurb: The Nissan GT-R is a sports car, built by Japanese marque Nissan from 2007 to 2025. It has a 2+2 seating layout and is also considered a grand tourer. The engine is front-mid mounted and drives all four wheels. It succeeded the Nissan Skyline GT-R, a high-performance variant of the Nissan Skyline.

title: Nissan Skyline GT-R
blurb: The Nissan Skyline GT-R is a Japanese grand tourer based on the Nissan Skyline range. The first cars named "Skyline GT-R" were produced between 1969 and 1972 under the model code KPGC10, and were successful in Japanese touring car racing events.

title: Party bike
about: Vehicle powered by multiple people pedaling
blurb: A party bike, conference bike, pedal pub, fietscafé, bierfiets, beer bike or bar bike is a multi-passenger human powered vehicle that is powered by the passengers.

title: Peel P50
blurb: The Peel P50 is a three-wheeled microcar originally made from 1962 to 1965 by the Peel Engineering Company on the Isle of Man, and then from 2010 to present. It was listed in the 2010 Guinness World Records as the smallest production car ever made.

title: Penny-farthing
blurb: The Victorian bicycle with one enormous front wheel and one tiny rear one.

title: Phaeton
blurb: A phaeton is a sporty open carriage popular in the late eighteenth and early nineteenth century. Drawn by one or two horses, a phaeton typically features a minimal very lightly sprung body atop four extravagantly large wheels.

title: Pontiac Firebird
blurb: The Pontiac Firebird is an American automobile built and produced by Pontiac from the 1967 to 2002 model years. Designed as a pony car to compete with the Ford Mustang, it was introduced on February 23, 1967, five months after GM's Chevrolet division's platform-sharing Camaro.

title: Porsche 911
blurb: A rear-engined sports car whose silhouette has barely changed since 1964.

title: Premier Padmini
about: Saloon made in India from 1964 to 2001
blurb: A Fiat 1100 built under licence in India from 1964 to 2001, renamed in 1974 after a 14th-century Rajput princess, and long the black-and-yellow taxi of Mumbai.

title: Proa
blurb: Proas are various types of multi-hull outrigger sailboats of the Austronesian peoples. The terms were used for native Austronesian ships in European records during the Colonial era indiscriminately, and thus can confusingly refer to the double-ended single-outrigger boats of Oceania, the…

title: Reed boat
blurb: Reed boats and rafts, along with dugout canoes and other rafts, are among the oldest known types of boats. Often used as traditional fishing boats, they are still used in a few places around the world, though they have generally been replaced with planked boats.

title: Road bicycle
about: Bicycles designed for traveling at speed on paved roads
blurb: The term road bicycle is used to describe bicycles built for traveling at speed on paved roads. Some sources use the term to mean racing bicycle.

title: Royal Enfield Bullet
blurb: The Royal Enfield Bullet is an overhead valve, single-cylinder, four-stroke motorcycle initially made by Royal Enfield in Redditch, Worcestershire England.

title: Sampan
about: Form of boat from Southeast Asia
blurb: A sampan is a relatively flat-bottomed wooden boat found in East, Southeast, and South Asia. It is possibly of Chinese or Austronesian origin. Some sampans include a small shelter on board and may be used as a permanent habitation on inland waters.

title: Sewn boat
blurb: A sewn boat is a type of wooden boat which has its planks sewn, stitched, tied, or bound together with natural fibre rope tendons or flexible wood, such as roots and willow branches.

title: Shaft-driven bicycle
about: Type of bicycle which uses a drive shaft to transmit power instead of a chain
blurb: A shaft-driven bicycle is a bicycle that uses a drive shaft instead of a chain to transmit power from the pedals to the wheel. Shaft drives were introduced in the 1880s, but were mostly supplanted by chain-driven bicycles due to the gear ranges possible with sprockets and derailleurs.

title: Shikara
about: Wooden boat of Dal Lake, Kashmir
blurb: A wooden boat of the lakes of Srinagar, usually seating six, with the boatman paddling at the back: the gondola of Kashmir.

title: Skipjack
about: Sailboat type used on Chesapeake Bay for oyster dredging
blurb: The skipjack is a traditional fishing boat used on the Chesapeake Bay for oyster dredging. It is a sailboat which succeeded the bugeye as the chief oystering boat on the bay, and it remains in service due to laws restricting the use of powerboats in the Maryland state oyster fishery.

title: Skyhook balloon
blurb: Skyhook balloons were high-altitude balloons developed by Otto C. Winzen and General Mills, Inc. They were used by the United States Navy Office of Naval Research in the late 1940s and 1950s for atmospheric research, especially for constant-level meteorological observations at very high altitudes.

title: Smart
blurb: Smart is a Swiss born-German automotive marque established in 1994 and currently operating as Smart Automobile Co., Ltd., a joint venture formed in 2019 by Mercedes-Benz AG and Zhejiang Geely Holding Group, aimed at manufacturing Smart-badged cars in China to be marketed globally.

title: Step-through frame
blurb: A step-through frame is a type of bicycle frame, often used for utility bicycles, with a low or absent top tube or cross-bar.

title: Tesla Cybercab
blurb: The Tesla Cybercab is a two-passenger battery-electric robotaxi manufactured by Tesla, Inc. for its Robotaxi ride-hailing service.

title: Tesla Cybertruck
blurb: The Tesla Cybertruck is a battery-electric full-size pickup truck manufactured by Tesla, Inc. since 2023. It was presented as a prototype concept in November 2019, with an angular design composed of flat, unpainted stainless steel body panels, drawing comparisons to low-polygon computer models.

title: Tesla Model S
blurb: The Tesla Model S is a battery-electric, four-door full-size car that the American automaker Tesla produced from 2012 to 2026. The automaker's second vehicle, the Model S has been described as one of the most influential electric cars in the industry.

title: Touring bicycle
about: Bicycle designed or modified for touring
blurb: A touring bicycle is a bicycle designed or modified to handle bicycle touring. To make the bikes sufficiently robust, comfortable and capable of carrying heavy loads, special features may include a long wheelbase, frame materials that favor flexibility over rigidity, heavy duty wheels, and multiple…

title: Toyota Hilux
blurb: The Toyota Hilux, stylised as HiLux and historically as Hi-Lux, is a series of pickup trucks produced and marketed by the Japanese automobile manufacturer Toyota. The majority of these vehicles are sold as a pickup truck or cab chassis, although they could be configured in a variety of body styles.

title: Toyota Land Cruiser
about: Series of four-wheel drive vehicles produced by Toyota
blurb: The Toyota Land Cruiser, also sometimes spelt as LandCruiser, is a series of four-wheel drive vehicles produced by the Japanese automobile manufacturer Toyota. It is Toyota's longest running series of models.

title: Troika
about: Carriage pulled by three beasts of burden
blurb: A troika is a high-speed Russian harness driving combination, using three horses abreast. In a common perception, a troika is pulling a sleigh, but this type of harness may also be used for wheeled carriages.

title: Tumbrel
blurb: A tumbrel is a two-wheeled cart or wagon typically designed to be hauled by a single horse or ox. Their original use was for agricultural work; in particular they were associated with carrying manure. Their most infamous use was taking prisoners to the guillotine during the French Revolution.

title: Umiak
blurb: The umiak, umialak, umiaq, umiac, oomiac, oomiak, ongiuk, or anyak is a type of open skin boat, used by the Yupik and Inuit, and was originally found in all coastal areas from Siberia to Greenland.

title: Vardo
about: Traditional horse-drawn wagon of the Romanichal
blurb: A vardoon, Gypsy wagon, living wagon, caravan, van and house-on-wheels) is a four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle traditionally used by travelling Romanichal as their home. The name vardo is a Romani term believed to have originated from the Ossetic wærdon meaning cart or carriage.

title: Vespa
blurb: The Italian scooter of 1946, whose name means wasp, built for nipping through narrow streets.

title: Victoria
blurb: The Victoria is a four-wheeled carriage with a coachman's seat in front and a folding hood over the passengers. Developed in France where it was named Victoria in honor of Queen Victoria, it was imported to Britain around 1869.

title: Vis-à-vis
blurb: Vis-à-vis has two meanings in carriage driving: a general seating arrangement with passengers sitting face-to-face, and a specific narrow carriage for just two passengers.

title: Volkswagen Beetle
blurb: The round, rear-engined people's car, built for 65 years and in over 21 million examples.

title: Waka
blurb: Waka are Māori watercraft, usually canoes ranging in size from small, unornamented canoes used for fishing and river travel to large, decorated war canoes up to 40 metres long.

title: Wheelie bike
about: Type of stylized children's bicycle designed in the 1960s
blurb: A wheelie bike, also called a dragster, muscle bike, high-riser, spyder bike or banana bike, is a type of stylized children's bicycle designed in the 1960s to resemble a chopper motorcycle and characterized by ape hanger handlebars, a banana seat with sissy bar, and small) wheels.

title: Yamaha MT-09
blurb: The Yamaha MT-09 is a street motorcycle of the MT series with an 847–890 cc liquid-cooled four-stroke 12-valve DOHC inline-three engine with crossplane crankshaft and a lightweight cast alloy frame. For 2018, the bike is now designated MT-09 in all markets.

title: Yamaha RX 100
blurb: The Yamaha RX 100 was a two-stroke motorcycle made by Yamaha from 1985 to 1996 with technical collaboration and distributed in India by the Escorts Group. The RX100 was known for its agility and acceleration. At the initial stage, Yamaha Japan was exporting all bikes from Japan to India.

title: Yamaha YZF-R1
blurb: The Yamaha YZF-R1, or simply R1, is a 998 cc sports motorcycle of the YZF-R series made by Yamaha. It was first released in 1998, undergoing significant updates in 2000, 2002, 2004, 2006, 2007, 2009, 2015, 2018 and 2020.

title: Yamaha YZF-R6
blurb: The Yamaha YZF-R6 is a sport bike, produced by Yamaha as a 600 class from 1999 to 2020. From 2021, production availability is limited to a non-homologated race-only specification in most global markets, causing race organizers to realign their engine eligibility criteria to encourage other…

title: Yangwang U9
blurb: The Yangwang U9 is a battery electric super-coupe manufactured by BYD Auto under its luxury car brand Yangwang. The U9 is the second vehicle from the Yangwang brand after the U8 off-road SUV, and was formally introduced on Auto Shanghai in April 2023.
